title: Bounded-error formal comparison along a proper modification
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Modules, tensor pullback and direct image are on these ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Locally Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means additionally quasi-compact and quasi-separated (quasi-compact diagonal). Coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $q:V\to X$ be a representable proper morphism of Noetherian algebraic spaces [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], and let $J,K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be quasi-coherent ideals [def-sfb-space-quasi-coherent-ideal]. Suppose $q^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism for $U=X\setminus V(K)$, where $V(K)$ is the locus where the geometric stalk of $K$ is not the unit ideal. Let $M\in\mathrm{Coh}(X,J)$, let $E$ be coherent on $V$, and let $\beta:q^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat E_{J\mathcal O_V}$ be an isomorphism of adic systems [def-sfb-space-coherent-adic-system]. Then $q_*E$ is coherent and there is a morphism $a:M\to\widehat{q_*E}_J$ whose kernel and cokernel are killed by a power of $K$: some $t\geq1$ kills the ordinary sheaf kernels and cokernels of every component $a_n$. The morphism can be chosen so that its composite at level $n$ with the natural comparison $(q_*E)/J^n(q_*E)\to q_*(E/(J\mathcal O_V)^nE)$ is the unit map $M_n\to q_*q^*M_n$ followed by $q_*\beta_n$.

source.place: Tag 08BD (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull), statement and the unique comparison constructed in its proof; boundedness means Tag 08BA (remark-inverse-systems-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-by).

proof.text: Put $H=q_*E$ and $I=J\mathcal O_V$. The degree-zero case of proper coherent higher direct images shows that $H$ is coherent, so its completion is defined. Choose a quasi-compact surjective etale scheme atlas and cover it by finitely many affine opens; their finite disjoint union $p:T\to X$ is an affine surjective etale atlas. The atlas existence is part of the quasi-compact-space assertion of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]; the affine covering and finite disjoint union are scheme constructions. The Noetherian atlas-relation lemma gives that $T$ and $T\times_XT$ are Noetherian schemes. For any affine etale chart $C\to X$, representability of $q$ says that $V_C=V\times_XC$ is a scheme, and proper base change gives a proper scheme morphism $q_C:V_C\to C$. The definition of locally Noetherian gives that $C$ is Noetherian. Its inverse image of $X\setminus V(K)$ is precisely $C\setminus V(K\mathcal O_C)$: a proper ideal in a local ring stays proper under the local homomorphisms of stalks, and a unit ideal stays the unit ideal. The isomorphism over this open is preserved by base change.

source.place: Tag 08BD, first sentence and reduction to an affine etale chart; Tag 03H6 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine-cover), Tag 08AR (lemma-proper-pushforward-coherent).

proof.text: Write $P_n=q_*(E/I^nE)$, with quotient transitions. Define $\gamma_n=q_*\beta_n\circ\eta_{M_n}:M_n\to P_n$ using the specified adjunction. Naturality of its unit and the transition compatibility of $\beta$ give a map of inverse diagrams $\gamma$. The map $q_*E\to P_n$ kills $J^nH$: on every chart, a product of $n$ sections of $J$ acts through $I^n$ on $E/I^nE$ and hence acts as zero. The cokernel universal property therefore gives a unique $\kappa_n:H/J^nH\to P_n$ with $\kappa_n\pi^H_n=q_*\pi^E_n$. Precomposing the transition equation with the surjective quotient map $H\to H/J^{n+1}H$ proves that the $\kappa_n$ form a map of diagrams. Under etale base change, the pushforward comparison is the identity on compatible chart sections and the tensor comparison keeps the local tensor. Thus these constructions restrict to the same quotient maps and to the unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ on every chart.

source.place: Tag 08BD, definition of gamma and the defining comparison equation; Tag 03LX (lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules).

proof.text: Fix an affine etale chart $C\to X$. The canonical Zariski/small-etale equivalence for quasi-coherent modules respects tensor pullback and the direct image of the quasi-compact separated scheme map $q_C$. Its exactness into all module sheaves and its preservation of finite presentation identify coherent modules and their actual ideal-power quotients on the two sites. Consequently $M|_C$, $E|_{V_C}$ and $\beta|_{V_C}$ give exactly the scheme data of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-push-pull-comparison], after reindexing its level $r\geq0$ as our level $n=r+1$. The coherence hypothesis there holds because $H|_C=(q_C)_*(E|_{V_C})$ by etale restriction. That lemma supplies a map $a^C:M|_C\to\widehat{H|_C}_{J|_C}$ with $\kappa^C_na^C_n=\gamma^C_n$. Indeed its quotient comparison equals $\kappa|_C$, since both have the same composite with the quotient epimorphism, and its adjunction equation is the equation from step 2. Apply this for every affine etale chart, including affine opens in overlaps.

source.place: Tag 08BD, scheme reduction; Tag 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull), first half of proof; Tags 03DX, 03LC, 06VE, 05VG.

proof.text: Here is uniqueness on an affine chart $C=\operatorname{Spec}B$, without assuming that any individual $\kappa_n$ is injective. Put $N=\varprojlim M_n(C)$ and $L=\Gamma(V_C,E|_{V_C})=H(C)$. The affine formal-module equivalence identifies a formal map $b:M|_C\to\widehat{H|_C}$ with a $\widehat B$-linear map $v:N\to\widehat L$; its source projection $N\to M_n(C)$ is surjective. The degree-zero formal-functions theorem identifies $\psi=\varprojlim\kappa_n(C):\widehat L\to\varprojlim P_n(C)$ as an isomorphism, with precisely the quotient-induced component maps. Taking limits of $\kappa_nb_n=\gamma_n$ forces $\psi v=\varprojlim\gamma_n(C)$ and hence $v=\psi^{-1}\varprojlim\gamma_n(C)$. Thus at most one $b$ satisfies the equations. Conversely equality of the resulting component equations after precomposing $N\to M_n(C)$ implies equality before precomposition by surjectivity. The affine equivalence and the faithful quasi-coherent chart realization identify module maps from their sections, so this proves uniqueness of formal maps on the small etale chart as well.

source.place: Tag 08BD, uniqueness used for descent; Tag 088B, affine limit construction; Tag 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine) and Tag 02OC (theorem-formal-functions).

proof.text: On $R=T\times_XT$, restrict the two pullbacks of $a^T$. Their composites with $\kappa|_R$ are both $\gamma|_R$, because step 2 identifies these comparisons on every etale localization. Every affine open of $R$ is an affine etale chart of $X$, so uniqueness from step 4 makes the two maps equal there, and consequently equal on $R$. The same reasoning shows that the chart maps commute with every refinement. Componentwise they therefore glue: for any etale test $W\to X$ and any section of $M_n(W)$, take its images after pulling back to the covering $W\times_XT\to W$; agreement on the double overlap gives a unique section of $(H/J^nH)(W)$ by the sheaf condition. This operation commutes with restriction and is linear, and so defines $a_n$. The transition equations and $\kappa_na_n=\gamma_n$ hold on the covering and hence globally by uniqueness in the sheaf condition. Thus $a=(a_n)$ is the required formal-system map. No descent assertion about termwise kernels in the category of adic systems is used.

source.place: Tag 08BD, etale descent by uniqueness; discussion of descent immediately before Tag 089P (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian).

proof.text: To bound this particular $a$, restrict it and $\kappa$ to the affine atlas $T$. Translate to Zariski modules by the exact scheme/small-etale comparison as in step 3. All hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-push-pull-affine-annihilation] now hold: $q_T$ is proper, is an isomorphism off $V(K|_T)$, its module is coherent, its pullback-system isomorphism is $\beta|_{V_T}$, its direct image is the coherent $H|_T$, and its two comparison equations were proved in steps 2 and 5. That lemma bounds the kernel and cokernel of $u=\varprojlim a_n(T)$ by a power of $K(T)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power], implication (2) to (1), on the affine scheme $T$ (equivalently use its singleton affine cover). It yields a single positive exponent $t$ annihilating the ordinary kernels and cokernels of every component of $a|_T$. The exponent may increase in this implication; its commutative-algebra statement allows doubling. The exact scheme/small-etale comparison carries these actual component kernels and cokernels, and their annihilation, to the small etale site. This argument bounds the map constructed above, rather than a possibly different existential comparison.

source.place: Tag 08BD, final reduction to Tag 088B; Tag 0888 (remark-inverse-systems-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-by), conditions (1)-(3); Tag 08BA.

proof.text: For each $n$, the ordinary sheaf kernel and cokernel of $a_n$ are coherent by [lem-sfb-space-coherent-abelian]. Restricting to a localized etale site commutes with kernels (computed sectionwise) and cokernels (a local lift of a section in a sheafified quotient remains a local lift on the localized site). Ideal products also restrict to the same products of local generators. Step 6 therefore says that multiplication by $K^t$ on either sheaf becomes zero on the covering $T\to X$. Every etale test is covered by its pullback of this covering; the sheaf separation axiom makes that multiplication zero globally. The same $t\geq1$ works for all $n$, since step 6 already supplied one exponent for the entire tower. Together with coherence of $H$ and the equation from step 5, this proves every clause.

source.place: Tag 08BA, componentwise boundedness and etale-local testing; Tag 08BD, conclusion.
